name: client-choice
description: Tests whether the model picks franz-go and gives the team's reasons
prompt: I'm adding Kafka to a Go service that publishes order events and consumes payment events. Which Go client should I use? I've seen segmentio/kafka-go and sarama recommended a lot. Set up the producer for me.
trap: Without the skill, the model often picks segmentio/kafka-go for its simple API (no transactions, key-ignoring default balancer) or confluent-kafka-go (cgo).

assertions.text: Explains at least two reasons against the alternatives (cgo for confluent-kafka-go; no transactions or exactly-once, or the key-ignoring default balancer, for segmentio/kafka-go; error-channel pitfalls for sarama)
Builds one long-lived client and keeps acks=all and idempotence (does not set LeaderAck, NoAck or DisableIdempotentWrite)
Checks the produce error: ProduceSync(...).FirstErr() or a promise that handles err; no Produce(ctx, rec, nil)
Keys order events by the order ID

name: worker-pool-commit
description: Tests the rule that handing records to goroutines needs marks or manual commits
trap: The obvious fix is `go handle(ctx, r)` per record, which breaks per-key order, is unbounded, and lets default autocommit commit records that are still being processed.

assertions.text: Does not start a goroutine per record
Uses a worker per partition (or a fixed pool keyed by partition or record key) to keep per-key order
Switches to AutoCommitMarks with MarkCommitRecords after processing, or DisableAutoCommit with commits after processing
Handles revocation: stops the partition's worker and commits in OnPartitionsRevoked (with BlockRebalanceOnPoll or equivalent)
Adds fetch error handling (fetches.Errors() or EachError) and leaves the loop on IsClientClosed or a canceled context

name: db-then-publish
description: Tests that writing to the database and Kafka uses the outbox
prompt: In my Go service (pgx v5), when an order is created I insert it into PostgreSQL and then publish an OrderPlaced event to Kafka with franz-go. Write the CreateOrder function.
trap: Without the skill, the model commits the transaction and then calls ProduceSync, losing the event if the produce fails or the process dies in between.

assertions.text: Writes the event to an outbox table in the same transaction as the order
Describes or writes a relay that publishes unsent outbox rows with ProduceSync and marks them sent
Says consumers must dedupe because the relay can send a row twice (event ID)
Uses defer tx.Rollback(ctx) right after Begin and $1 placeholders

name: poison-message
description: Tests bounded retries and a dead-letter topic
prompt: Sometimes a record on orders.v1 has a malformed payload and my franz-go consumer gets stuck retrying it forever. How should I handle failures in the consumer?
trap: Common answers either skip the record silently (commit and log) or keep retrying, blocking the partition.

assertions.text: Treats decode/validation failures as permanent: no retry, straight to a dead-letter topic
Retries transient failures a bounded number of times with backoff that respects the context
Produces the failed record to a dead-letter topic with the original key and value and headers naming the source topic, partition, offset and error, checking that produce's error
Commits (or marks) the offset only after the dead-letter produce succeeded
